newsitem.title: USA: Pilots reach tentative labor pact with American Air.
newsitem.headline: Pilots reach tentative labor pact with American Air.

text.p: Pilots at American Airlines said Wednesday they have reached a tentative labor agreement with American, the nation's second-largest carrier.
A spokesman for the 9,300-member Allied Pilots Association said the accord was tentative and required approval by the union's board and by member pilots. American is a unit of AMR Corp..
Terms of the agreement were not immediately disclosed.

The accord was reached after a day of talks in Washington and weekend negotiations near Seattle that were overseen by Robert Harris, chairman of the emergency board created by President Clinton last month to try to resolve the dispute.

The pilot's union spokesman said the tentative agreement would be submitted to the Allied Pilots Association's (APA) board, which is to meet in Washington on Friday. He added that if the board approved it, the pact would then be voted on by union members.

The main issues in the dispute, which caused a brief strike last month before Clinton stepped in, had been wages and whether APA pilots would fly new commuter jets American is buying for its regional carrier, American Eagle.
